environment.cpu: Intel Core i9-11900KF (8 cores, 16 threads), CPU E-steps use all hardware threads
environment.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 (8 GiB), driver 590.48.01, subgroup 32, shader float64
environment.display: Xephyr :7 (nested X server), 64x64 window, VSync off, validation layers off

why_rerun: The independent review (Fable 5.1, Codex 6 Astra) showed fp32 kernel terms can lose ~1e-4 relative accuracy on inputs the seam routed to the device (narrow kernels with far rows or large coordinates). The fix routes iterations whose first-order fp32 error estimate exceeds 2e-5 to the exact CPU dense pass; that changes which iterations run on the device, so the scaling profile was repeated.

outcomes.rigid_100000_points: Vulkan 114.6 s vs CPU twin 186.1 s (1.62x), Auto 187.6 s, Nystroem 121.2 s, dense 411.7 s; 9 of 48 iterations on the device (21 before the guard)
outcomes.rigid_10000_points: Vulkan 829 ms vs CPU twin 1312 ms (1.58x), Nystroem 1061 ms; 10 of 35 on the device
outcomes.rigid_1000_points: Vulkan 57 ms vs CPU twin 28 ms: frame latency dominates
outcomes.parity: max registered-point delta to the CPU twin 6.6e-12 (10^5); RMS to the ground truth equal

limitations: The guard takes the worst row over the whole target (the fixture's 5% uniform clutter rows make it strict), so most mid-sigma iterations run the CPU dense pass; per-row routing is METHOD-063. One host, one GPU, one rigid fixture.
not_measured: Nonrigid and Bayesian device runs; memory peak; other GPUs.
